title: Ramp resilience runway and SLA escape hatch
summary: A compact operational blueprint for stepwise traffic ramp, resilience checks, and an explicit SLA escape hatch decision checklist for launches that risk violating latency or availability SLOs. Designed for product-ops + SRE + on-call owners to run during day-0 and first 72 hours.
body:
Purpose:
This doc codifies a lightweight but rigorous ramp and resilience runway with explicit KPI thresholds and an "escape hatch" decision checklist to protect customer SLAs during initial traffic ramp and abnormal degradation. It is intended to be used in the launch war room and as an attachable runbook for canary and staged rollouts.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted Redwood API endpoints and Dedicated pools where we control routing policies.
- Focused on first 72 hours after incremental traffic shifts >10% or feature flags that change routing/quotas.
- Assumes baseline observability is in place: per-route latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), error rates, queue depth, token-per-second throughput, and cost-per-token.

Key KPIs and operational thresholds (actionable):
- Availability (5m window): target >= 99.95%; yellow if <99.9%; red if <99.5%.
- P95 latency (in ms): target <= 220ms; yellow if >300ms; red if >500ms.
- Error rate (5xx + 4xx from system): target <= 0.2%; yellow if >0.5%; red if >1.5%.
- SLA burn-rate index: measured as (observed-error-weighted-penalty / SLA-budget). Escalate when burn-rate > 2x in 1 hour.
- Cost-per-1000-tokens shift: flag if >+30% vs expected plan during ramp.

Ramp phases (typical):
- Phase 0 — Canary (1% traffic, 10–30 min observation): verify correctness, basic perf, logs look normal.
- Phase 1 — Early ramp (5% traffic, 30–60 min): validate throughput, KV cache hit ratio, and memory pressure.
- Phase 2 — Medium ramp (20% traffic, 60–90 min): observe autoscale behavior and latency tail behavior.
- Phase 3 — Wide ramp (50% traffic, 2–4 hours): watch inter-region fallbacks and routing jitter.
- Phase 4 — Full (100% or target allocation): sustained monitoring and handoff to steady-state SRE.

For each phase run the following quick checks within the window:
- Telemetry sanity: no sudden gaps in metrics ingestion.
- CPU/GPU saturation: <85% sustained on serving nodes (yellow at 85-95%, red >95%).
- KV cache hit rate: no >10% drop vs baseline.
- Queue depth and tail latency: p99 should remain within 1.8x of pre-ramp baseline.
- Token generation per request distribution: check for outliers indicating prompt regressions.

Traffic stress scenarios and mitigations (fast checklist):
- Scenario A: P95 jumps >300ms but errors stable.
  Mitigation: Pause ramp, reduce batch sizes for affected model variant, shift a fraction of traffic to cheaper/lower-latency variant, and attach extra tracing.
- Scenario B: Error rate increases >0.5% with client-visible 5xx.
  Mitigation: Immediate rollback to previous deployment or reduce traffic to last-known-good percentage; enable automatic fallback routing to dedicated lower-capacity pool.
- Scenario C: Cost-per-token jumps >30% and throughput is fine.
  Mitigation: Re-evaluate quantization profile, reduce concurrency caps, and enable request-level caching for repeated prefixes.
- Scenario D: Node OOM or GPU memory pressure.
  Mitigation: Exclude affected nodes from LB, scale up node count (if autoscale possible), or revert model variant to smaller/quantized variant.

SLA escape hatch decision checklist (binary checkpoints — yes/no):
- Is current availability below red threshold? (Y/N)
- Is current p95 latency above red threshold? (Y/N)
- Is error burn-rate > 2x in 1h or 1.5x in 15m? (Y/N)
- Has on-call SRE confirmed systemic root signal (not client misbehavior)? (Y/N)
- Are automated rollbacks configured and tested for this route? (Y/N)
If two or more answers are Y => execute escape hatch: reduce live allocation to last-known-good, open urgent incident (INC-xxx), notify customers in affected tiers via status.redwood.ai page and CS lead.

Escalation actions on escape hatch (ordered):
1) Immediate traffic reallocation: shift 60-80% of traffic back to last-known-good model/revision.
2) Trigger autoscaling policy to burst capacity if safe and within budget.
3) If traffic reallocation and burst fail to restore SLA within 10 minutes, initiate controlled rollback to previous routing policy and pause new deployments.
4) Notify Product/CS for customer comms and message scoreboard.

Roles & owners (default):
- Launch lead: Product-ops owner (Maya Patel). Responsible for phase gating decisions.
- SRE on-call: Primary for operational mitigations and node-level actions.
- Serving runtime engineer: model variant and quantization rollback.
- Console/Observability owner: confirm metric integrity and assist with traces.
- Customer success: draft customer update if customers are or will be impacted.

Runbook snippets (copy/paste friendly):
- Pause ramp: /ops/ramp pause --route <route> --reason "latency-breach"
- Rollback route: /ops/route rollback --route <route> --to-revision <rev-id>
- Reallocate traffic: /ops/route split --route <route> --alloc "revA:20,revB:80"
- Enable fallback: /ops/fallback enable --route <route> --variant <fallback-variant>

Communication play (war-room):
- Channel: #launch-warroom (persistent). Use pinned message template with KPI table snap.
- Status cadence: 0/15/30/60 minute updates during early ramp then hourly.
- External: if escape hatch executed, CS drafts incident notice within 30 minutes; customer-facing timeline and mitigation steps within 90 minutes.

Post-launch telemetry capture and artifacts to attach to handoff:
- 72-hour rolling windows of: latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), error taxonomy, cost per token, autoscale events, GC/eviction logs.
- Top 10 traces for p99 requests and top 20 error stack traces.
- Change list: commits/PRs that were in effect at launch window.

Open questions and followups (owner tags):
- (Ethan) Validate that rollback orchestration supports cross-region reallocation without double-billing.
- (Priya) Add automated alert for KV-cache-hit delta > 8% during ramps.
- (Liam) Create a lightweight dashboard widget for escape hatch triggers (one-click snapshot export).

Appendix: Short example KPI watch matrix (for the war-room)
- row: metric, pre-launch baseline, yellow threshold, red threshold, current value (fill live)
- Availability: 99.99%, 99.9%, 99.5%, --
- P95 latency: 210ms, 300ms, 500ms, --
- Error rate: 0.08%, 0.5%, 1.5%, --
- SLA burn-rate: 0.6x, 1x, 2x, --

Notes: Keep this doc attached to the launch ticket and link the escape-hatch runbook into the CI/CD pipeline gates. This is intentionally concise — expand with route-specific numbers when copied into the product release card.
